newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-AWARD WINNER SAMMER HOPES TO GET EVEN BETTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AWARD WINNER SAMMER HOPES TO GET EVEN BETTER.

text.p: Matthias Sammer, winner of the Golden Ball as the 1996 European footballer of the year, said on Tuesday he believes he can become an even better player.

The Borussia Dortmund libero, who helped Germany to win the European championship in June and his club to secure the Bundesliga title, also said in an interview with Bild daily he had not expected the honour because he was injured for nearly two months.

"It was an absolute surprise for me," Sammer said of the award announced on Monday. "I didn't expect it. The European championship brought a lot of recognition for me, but I was injured for seven weeks this year."

Sammer, the first defender to win the award since Franz Beckenbauer and the fifth German, said he thought he might finish in the top five. He hopes to go through an entire year without injuries and improve the consistency of his performance.

"I am not at the pinnacle," he said. "I lack consistency. I hope to one day be able to make a proper preparation for a season, train without injuries and play permanently. Players are at the top of their game when they get a rhythm."
Sammer, 28, said he has no plans to retire soon.
"You can never believe that you have reached the peak," he said. "Self-criticism is the basis for success. Every championship is the reward for hard work."
